svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Four ways a new species can form. Each dot is an individual; colour shows its genetic make-up."], [1, "Gene flow is reduced or stopped between groups."], [3, "Over many generations, mutation, natural selection and genetic drift make the groups different."], [10, "Eventually they are reproductively isolated: new species."]]
svg.title: Modes of speciation
svg.desc: Four panels: allopatric, peripatric, parapatric and sympatric speciation, with populations shown as dots that change colour as they diverge into new species.
svg.text: Dots: individuals. Colour change: genetic divergence over many generations.

g.data-info: A geographical barrier (river, mountains, sea) splits a population. With no gene flow, different mutations, natural selection and genetic drift make the two groups diverge until they can no longer interbreed.
A small group becomes isolated at the edge of the range (founder effect). Genetic drift is strong in a small population, so it can diverge quickly.
Neighbouring populations along an environmental gradient. Gene flow is limited, and selection differs at each end, so they diverge, often with a narrow hybrid zone.
A new species forms in the same area, with no geographical barrier: for example by polyploidy in plants, or by using different food or mating at different times.
g.text: e.g. polyploidy, different food or mating time
